what_this_lane_repairs.defect: Capper identity was derived as metadata.capper ?? metadata.submittedBy ?? pick.source. When no capper was recorded, an intake channel became a capper: CLV history, trust feedback and promotion scoring all aggregated under a string like 'smart-form'.
what_this_lane_repairs.why_it_is_not_merely_a_missing_null_chec: picks.capper_id is a real, existence-checked column. resolvePickForeignKeys (packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts:390) derives a candidate, then queries cappers.id and returns capperId: data?.id ?? null. So a NULL means 'this capper is not recognised by the cappers table', not 'nobody told us'. Falling back to source therefore overrides a deliberate refusal with a guess, and it does so in two independent wrong ways: it invents a capper out of a channel, and it merges every capper sharing a channel into one population.
what_this_lane_repairs.production_relevance_measured: Production zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm holds 107,862 picks. Exactly 16 carry a non-null capper_id, all of them griff843 via smart-form (10 validated, 6 settled). The other 107,846 are unattributed, and 18,280 of those are settled. Grouping those settled rows by the OLD expression COALESCE(metadata->>'capper', metadata->>'submittedBy', source) yields 7 synthetic identities, none of which is a capper: smart-form 8,360 settled, codex 7,763, t1-proof 2,145, utv2-803-final-proof 5, system:candidate-pick-scanner 4, canary-proof 2, api 1. The largest synthetic 'capper' in the system was the intake channel itself, and the second was an executor.

unit_tests.label: The whole promotion/edge integration suite at this head, including the 8 tests this lane adds: that resolveCapperIdentity reads the column and refuses to invent an identity; that two cappers sharing one intake channel keep separate CLV populations; that an intake channel cannot acquire a CLV history of its own; that unattributed picks never contribute to a real capper; that the unattributed sentinel is refused before any read rather than aggregated; that a persisted submission carries its capper identity on the column; that promotion reads the CLV history of the pick's capper rather than of its channel; and that a pick whose capper FK did not resolve gets no CLV adjustment. The 81 pre-existing tests are unchanged and still pass, so the suite cannot go green by relaxing promotion behaviour.

production_measurement.what_this_establishes: The fallback this lane removes is not a theoretical hazard. On production data it would mint 7 synthetic cappers out of 18,280 settled picks, the largest being a 'capper' named smart-form with 8,360 settled picks and the second an executor named codex with 7,763. Feeding either aggregate's CLV back into a trust score is the conflation the change removes, and the trust score it would have adjusted belongs to the only real capper in the table.
production_measurement.and_what_it_does_not: It does not establish that any capper statistic is correct today. Exactly one capper is attributed in production and only 6 of its picks are settled, all of them 2026-05-29 proof fixtures. Grouped capper statistics remain a later lane; this lane makes the grouping key honest, not the population real.

queries.label: settled population and settlement records available to the CLV path
queries.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM picks WHERE status = 'settled'), (SELECT count(*) FROM picks WHERE status = 'settled' AND capper_id IS NOT NULL), (SELECT count(*) FROM settlement_records)
queries.note: computeClvTrustAdjustment reads settlements and then the pick behind each one. With settled_attributed at zero, every one of those reads now resolves to the sentinel and is skipped, so no CLV adjustment can be manufactured from this population. Before the change the same 13,524 rows would have been partitioned into the three synthetic cappers above.

why_it_could_not_be_closed_inside_this_l: file_scope_lock is pinned at lane-start and admits exactly four paths — apps/api/src/capper-identity.ts, clv-feedback.ts, promotion-edge-integration.test.ts and promotion-service.ts. A new apps/api/src/t1-proof-*.test.ts file is not declarable here, and an agent cannot widen the lock.
Wiring any new test file into the t1-proof:live battery requires editing root package.json, which is also outside this lock.

Shadow Parity is path-triggered on apps/api/src/**/*promotion* and its assert-unmodified-vs-base pin list includes package.json, so a PR that both touches promotion-service.ts and edits package.json is refused. The two requirements are mutually exclusive inside one lane by construction, not by oversight.
coverage_gap.why_it_is_not_a_reason_to_hold_the_lane: The change is a refusal, not an acceptance: every path it alters either returns the real column value or returns null/sentinel. There is no branch that newly admits something. Against the staging population every pick resolves to the sentinel, so the only behaviour reachable there is the refusal, and the refusal is what the four mutations pin.
coverage_gap.disposition: Recorded as a dependency for a follow-up lane owning apps/api/src/t1-proof-utv2-1907-capper-attribution.test.ts plus the root package.json wiring. That lane touches no *promotion* path and therefore does not trigger Shadow Parity, which is why the coverage can exist there and cannot exist here.
